claims.text: Conventional EAM references cannot represent the full diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Replacing the EAM reference with an MLP trained on solid and liquid ab initio configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
An MLP trained on diverse solid and liquid configurations can represent the diverse atomic environments in both phases.
The MLP's many-body interaction terms capture local chemical order.
The MLP's many-body interaction terms capture medium-range chemical order.
The MLP's many-body interaction terms capture disordered liquid environments.
Capturing chemical order and disordered liquid environments bridges the configurational diversity between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Training on configurations typical of the ab initio liquid yields a more faithful description of short-range ordering.
Training on configurations typical of the ab initio liquid yields a more faithful description of mid-range ordering.
Conventional EAM models used in TOR-TILD are more rigid and less adaptable than the proposed MLP.
The MLP will reduce discontinuities in the thermodynamic-integration path relative to conventional EAM models.
MLP-based thermodynamic integration will produce free-energy differences closer to direct ab initio calculations than EAM-based integration.
Analogous elemental and binary studies indicate a potentially order-of-magnitude reduction in mismatch.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing at least four distinct elements near and at their melting temperatures.
The intervention requires high-quality ab initio training data spanning the relevant solid and liquid configurations.
